label: One-sample t-test
whenToUse: Compare one sample mean to a known/reference value when the outcome is approximately normal.
assumptions: Approximate normality in sample or large sample size
whatToReport: t statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value
resultsTemplate: A one-sample t-test showed that the mean [outcome] was [not] different from [reference], t(df) = X.XX, p = .XXX, 95% CI [LL, UL].
notes: Use Wilcoxon signed-rank if strong non-normality is present.

label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
whenToUse: Compare paired measurements or one-sample median difference when normality is not met.
assumptions: Paired/related data or one-sample difference scores
Symmetry of difference distribution is preferred
whatToReport: Median and IQR (or paired median difference)
W statistic (or V/Z depending on software) and p-value
resultsTemplate: A Wilcoxon signed-rank test indicated [no] median difference in [outcome], W = X, p = .XXX.
notes: For one-sample use, differences are tested against zero/reference median.

label: Independent t-test
whenToUse: Compare means between two independent groups when normality is reasonable and variances are similar.
whatToReport: t statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value
resultsTemplate: An independent t-test found that [Group A] had [higher/lower/similar] [outcome] than [Group B], t(df) = X.XX, p = .XXX, 95% CI [LL, UL].

label: Welch t-test
whenToUse: Compare means between two independent groups when variances are unequal.
whatToReport: Welch t statistic, adjusted df, and p-value
resultsTemplate: A Welch t-test showed [Group A] and [Group B] differed [not] in [outcome], t(df_welch) = X.XX, p = .XXX.
notes: Preferred over classic t-test when variances differ.

label: Mann–Whitney U test
whenToUse: Compare two independent groups when normality is violated or outcome is ordinal.
assumptions: Similar distribution shapes if interpreted as median difference
whatToReport: U statistic (and Z if provided) with p-value
resultsTemplate: A Mann–Whitney U test indicated [no] difference between groups on [outcome], U = X, p = .XXX.

label: Paired t-test
whenToUse: Compare means from two related measurements (e.g., pre/post) when differences are approximately normal.
whatToReport: Mean difference and SD of differences
Confidence interval for paired mean difference
resultsTemplate: A paired t-test showed a [significant/non-significant] change in [outcome], t(df) = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: One-way ANOVA
whenToUse: Compare means across three or more independent groups when assumptions are met.
whatToReport: F statistic with df and p-value
Effect size (e.g., eta-squared or partial eta-squared)
resultsTemplate: A one-way ANOVA found [a/no] group effect on [outcome], F(df1, df2) = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: Welch ANOVA
whenToUse: Compare means across three or more independent groups when variances are unequal.
whatToReport: Welch F statistic with adjusted df and p-value
resultsTemplate: A Welch ANOVA indicated [a/no] group difference in [outcome], F_welch(df1, df2) = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: Kruskal–Wallis test
whenToUse: Compare three or more independent groups for non-normal or ordinal outcomes.
assumptions: Similar distribution shapes for median interpretation
whatToReport: Post hoc pairwise tests with multiplicity correction
resultsTemplate: A Kruskal–Wallis test showed [a/no] group difference in [outcome], H(df) = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: Repeated-measures ANOVA
whenToUse: Compare means across three or more related conditions/time points under approximate normality.
whatToReport: F statistic with df and p-value
Sphericity test and correction (e.g., Greenhouse-Geisser) if violated
resultsTemplate: A repeated-measures ANOVA found [a/no] effect of condition on [outcome], F(df1, df2) = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: Friedman test
whenToUse: Compare three or more related conditions when normality is not met.
whatToReport: Friedman chi-square statistic, df, and p-value
Post hoc pairwise comparisons with correction
resultsTemplate: A Friedman test showed [a/no] difference across conditions for [outcome], χ²(df) = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: Chi-square test
whenToUse: Evaluate association or group differences between categorical variables with adequate expected counts.
resultsTemplate: A chi-square test found [an/no] association between [var1] and [var2], χ²(df) = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: Fisher’s exact test
whenToUse: Analyze categorical association for small expected counts, especially in 2x2 tables.
whatToReport: Odds ratio and confidence interval for 2x2 tables
resultsTemplate: Fisher’s exact test indicated [an/no] association between [var1] and [var2], p = .XXX.
notes: For larger-than-2x2 tables, consider Fisher-Freeman-Halton extension.

label: McNemar test
whenToUse: Compare paired binary outcomes (e.g., before/after yes/no).
whatToReport: Exact version if discordant counts are small
resultsTemplate: A McNemar test showed [a/no] change in paired binary outcomes, χ²(1) = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: Pearson correlation
whenToUse: Measure linear association between two continuous approximately normal variables.
resultsTemplate: Pearson correlation showed [a/no] linear association between [x] and [y], r = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: Spearman rank correlation
whenToUse: Measure monotonic association when normality is unclear or data are ordinal/non-normal.
resultsTemplate: Spearman correlation indicated [a/no] monotonic association between [x] and [y], ρ = X.XX, p = .XXX.

label: Linear regression
whenToUse: Model a continuous outcome using one or more predictors.
resultsTemplate: Linear regression indicated that [predictor] was [not] associated with [outcome], β = X.XX (SE = X.XX), p = .XXX.

label: Logistic regression
whenToUse: Model a categorical outcome (typically binary) from predictors.
assumptions: Binary outcome (or multinomial/ordinal variant as needed)
Linearity in the logit for continuous predictors
resultsTemplate: Logistic regression showed that [predictor] had [no] association with odds of [outcome], OR = X.XX, 95% CI [LL, UL], p = .XXX.
notes: Use binary logistic for two-category outcomes.

label: Poisson regression
whenToUse: Model count outcomes as rates/counts with log link.
resultsTemplate: Poisson regression indicated [predictor] was [not] associated with [count outcome], IRR = X.XX, 95% CI [LL, UL], p = .XXX.
notes: Check overdispersion; consider negative binomial if overdispersion is present.

label: Cox proportional hazards model
whenToUse: Model time-to-event outcomes with censoring.
whatToReport: Number of events and follow-up summary
resultsTemplate: A Cox model showed [predictor] had [no] association with hazard of [event], HR = X.XX, 95% CI [LL, UL], p = .XXX.
notes: Assess proportional hazards assumption (e.g., Schoenfeld residuals).
